title: Short-Termism in Democratic Policymaking
bottleneck: Elected governments discount the future heavily: research investments that pay off in decades lose to spending with immediate political returns. Long-horizon programs (fusion, space science, basic research) survive only through exceptional political entrepreneurship, and policy reversals strand multi-year efforts. Basic research with decadal payoffs is the first casualty of budget crunches and political turnover.
why_it_blocks: Democracies systematically underinvest in the future relative to what their citizens' long-term interests require. Each cancelled long-term program teaches researchers not to trust the next promise.
current_state: Independent research agencies with statutory independence partly insulate science, but they remain vulnerable to budget politics. Insulated, long-horizon funding institutions are the classic remedy, but they require political self-restraint to create. Political self-restraint to protect long-horizon institutions is rare but essential.
